description: Descriptive fact transcribed from the pinned source.

attributes.value: Average Pearson correlation between predicted and observed expression was 0.114 to 0.123 across the 6 kb models; the authors read this as limited information for predicting subject-specific tissue-level expression. name: Feng GTEx whole-blood expression prediction, all genes, 6 kb input
description: Table 4 gene-expression prediction on all 21,004 genes with ~6 kb input; Feng et al. 2025 source-reported protocol.

attributes.scope_note: Per-gene regression of covariate-corrected GTEx v8 whole-blood expression (residuals after regressing sex, PEER factors and genotype principal components) on frozen zero-shot embeddings of each subject's phased sequence around the transcription start site. One random forest regressor per gene; subjects split 75:25 into training and test; fivefold cross-validation on MSE for hyperparameter tuning. Pearson correlation and MSE between predicted and observed expression are computed per gene and averaged across genes. Random forest was chosen over XGBoost because it was better for every model (Supplementary Table 3). Supervised on expression labels; not label-free prediction.
attributes.task: Subject-level gene expression prediction from personal sequence (average per-gene Pearson correlation and MSE)
attributes.access_note: Individual-level GTEx v8 whole-genome sequences and expression are protected human-participant data: per the Data availability statement, raw individual WGS must be requested through the GTEx Protected Data Access portal, and the processed expression benchmark is not deposited with the other processed datasets on Hugging Face. Only aggregated GTEx releases are public.
attributes.reproducibility_note: Reproduction requires approved GTEx protected access, the per-model GPU environments described in the author README (pinned at 3f4c81ce066f3c47422a83466b085aac1a6be902), and scheduler-style job scripts that take a job index and placeholder dataset and checkpoint paths. The pinned job_scripts/gtex_hyena.py reads 'long_seqs_by_gene', centre-crops to 6000 bp and writes to an output folder named 'cadph_long'; which script settings produced each Table 4 row cannot be confirmed from the repository. Not attempted by Rewire.
attributes.comparison_limit: Not comparable with the long-input rows: those cover a 768-gene subset (Table 4 footnote).
attributes.hyperparameters: Random forest grid: n_estimators 100, 200, 500; max_depth None, 5, 10 (printed as Supplementary Table 5; the main text cites it as Supplementary Table 6).

name: Relevance of feng-dna-fm-20261013-protocol-gtex-wb-expression-6kb to "Select regulatory variants and genes for functional follow-up"
description: Descriptive fact transcribed from the pinned source.

attributes.value: feng-dna-fm-20261013-protocol-gtex-wb-expression-6kb
attributes.endpoint: Average per-gene Pearson correlation and MSE between predicted and observed whole-blood expression across GTEx subjects, from frozen embeddings of each subject's phased TSS-centred sequence plus a per-gene random forest
attributes.rationale: Proxy: tests whether a model's sequence representation captures inter-individual cis-sequence effects on expression, which bears on allele-effect prediction for a locus. It does not score individual variants, link elements to genes or measure perturbation outcomes, which the use case needs.
constraints: Inspect every linked evaluation's source locator before citing a result.
Do not combine this mapping's evaluations with any other protocol's results.
Compare rows only within this protocol.
limitations: Labels are covariate-corrected whole-blood expression of GTEx subjects, not allele-specific or endogenous perturbation effects, and not in the user's cell type.

Each model's representation is frozen; a random forest is fitted per gene on expression labels, so this measures how much expression variation the embedding plus a supervised head explains, not a label-free variant-effect score.
Individual-level GTEx data are protected (GTEx Protected Data Access application); the benchmark cannot be rerun from public data.
Transcribed from the paper; Feng et al. did not develop the models (independent_paper). No reproduction by Rewire and no human scientific review.
The authors call overall performance modest and say the findings should be considered preliminary indicators (Results, Gene expression prediction, last paragraph).
Subjects are split 75:25 within each gene; no loci, genes or studies are held out, which the use case's validation requirements ask for.
GROVER uses a 2,048 bp centre crop, so its input differs from the other four rows.
The ~6 kb TSS-centred window leaves out distal regulatory elements.
